predecessors.name: Ming dynasty
predecessors.text: the Ming lands Li Zicheng took: Xiangyang ('By 1643, Li had captured Xiangyang'), Xi'an and Shaanxi (late 1643), Taiyuan (March 1644) and Beijing (April 1644)

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: Beijing (6 June 1644), then Xi'an and Shaanxi when Li 'abandon[ed] his headquarters in Xi'an in February 1645'

successors.name: Southern Ming
successors.text: Hubei, where Li 'is generally believed to have died ... in 1645'; the Shun page: 'Surrender to the Southern Ming: 1646'

rulers.name: Li Zicheng (Yongchang Emperor from 1644)
rulers.title: Dashing King, then emperor of the Shun

ledger.x: 1643: Li Zicheng, in rebellion since 1629, holds Xiangyang.
1643: Li Zicheng takes Xi'an and Shaanxi.
1644: Li Zicheng founds the Great Shun at Xi'an.
1644: Li Zicheng's armies take Taiyuan and Shanxi.
1644: the Shun capital moves from Xi'an to Beijing.
1644: the Shun and Wu Sangui fight at Shanhai Pass.
1644: Li is beaten at Shanhai Pass.
1645: North China is the Qing's, bridging (by 1645).
1645: the Shun end as a territory.

wars.name: Battle of Shanhai Pass
wars.outcome: Wu Sangui opened the pass to the Manchus; Li's army was defeated on 27 May 1644 and Beijing was lost on 5-6 June.

wars.name: Late Ming peasant rebellions
wars.outcome: Li Zicheng rose at Mizhi in 1629, was destroyed in 1638, rebuilt his army in Henan from 1639, took Xiangyang (1643), Xi'an (late 1643) and Beijing (April 1644).

wars.name: Qing pursuit of the Shun
wars.outcome: Li was forced out of Xi'an in February 1645 and is thought to have died in Hubei that year.

certainty.note: A mobile rebel regime: the land held changes with the armies' positions; no page gives a boundary.
